# Searching

Linear queries over a slice in no particular order: whether it holds a value, where, and how many.

<h2 id="contains"><code>Contains&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Contains<T>(items: T[..], value: T) -> bool
```

Whether any element of `items` equals `value`.
`items` is borrowed and read; `value` is read by value. An empty slice contains nothing, so this is false.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length, stopping at the first match, and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Find.rux#L23)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description             |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `items` | `T[..]` | the sequence to work on |
| `value` | `T`     | the value to look for   |

**Returns**: whether any element equals `value`

<h2 id="count"><code>Count&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Count<T>(items: T[..], value: T) -> uint
```

How many elements of `items` equal `value`.
`items` is borrowed and read; `value` is read by value. An empty slice gives zero.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Find.rux#L35)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description             |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `items` | `T[..]` | the sequence to work on |
| `value` | `T`     | the value to look for   |

**Returns**: how many elements equal `value`

<h2 id="index-of"><code>IndexOf&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IndexOf<T>(items: T[..], value: T) -> uint?
```

The index of the first element of `items` equal to `value`.
`items` is borrowed and read; `value` is read by value. Reports `none` when no element matches, including for an
empty slice.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length, stopping at the first match, and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Find.rux#L56)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description             |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `items` | `T[..]` | the sequence to work on |
| `value` | `T`     | the value to look for   |

**Returns**: the first index holding `value`, or `none`

<h2 id="last-index-of"><code>LastIndexOf&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func LastIndexOf<T>(items: T[..], value: T) -> uint?
```

The index of the last element of `items` equal to `value`.
`items` is borrowed and read; `value` is read by value. Reports `none` when no element matches.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length, stopping at the first match from the end, and allocates
nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Find.rux#L74)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description             |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `items` | `T[..]` | the sequence to work on |
| `value` | `T`     | the value to look for   |

**Returns**: the last index holding `value`, or `none`

<h2 id="index-where"><code>IndexWhere&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IndexWhere<T>(items: T[..], predicate: func(T) -> bool) -> uint?
```

The index of the first element of `items` that `predicate` accepts.
`items` is borrowed and read; `predicate` is called once per element until it accepts one. Reports `none` when
it accepts none.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever `predicate` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Find.rux#L92)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type              | Description                     |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `items`     | `T[..]`           | the sequence to work on         |
| `predicate` | `func(T) -> bool` | the test each element is put to |

**Returns**: the first index whose element satisfies `predicate`, or `none`

<h2 id="last-index-where"><code>LastIndexWhere&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func LastIndexWhere<T>(items: T[..], predicate: func(T) -> bool) -> uint?
```

The index of the last element of `items` that `predicate` accepts.
`items` is borrowed and read; `predicate` is called once per element from the end until it accepts one. Reports

Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever `predicate` does.

<h2 id="count-where"><code>CountWhere&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func CountWhere<T>(items: T[..], predicate: func(T) -> bool) -> uint
```

How many elements of `items` the predicate accepts.
`items` is borrowed and read; `predicate` is called once per element. An empty slice gives zero.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever `predicate` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Find.rux#L127)

| Name | Description      |

| `T`  | the element type |

| Name        | Type              | Description                     |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `items`     | `T[..]`           | the sequence to work on         |
| `predicate` | `func(T) -> bool` | the test each element is put to |

**Returns**: how many elements satisfy `predicate`

<h2 id="all-of"><code>AllOf&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func AllOf<T>(items: T[..], predicate: func(T) -> bool) -> bool
```

Whether `predicate` accepts every element of `items`.
`items` is borrowed and read. An empty slice satisfies this, as it satisfies every universal claim: there is no
element that fails.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length, stopping at the first rejection, and allocates nothing
beyond whatever `predicate` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Find.rux#L149)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type              | Description                     |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `items`     | `T[..]`           | the sequence to work on         |
| `predicate` | `func(T) -> bool` | the test each element is put to |

**Returns**: whether every element satisfies `predicate`; true for an empty sequence

<h2 id="any-of"><code>AnyOf&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func AnyOf<T>(items: T[..], predicate: func(T) -> bool) -> bool
```

Whether `predicate` accepts at least one element of `items`.
`items` is borrowed and read. An empty slice does not satisfy this: there is no element that passes.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length, stopping at the first acceptance, and allocates nothing
beyond whatever `predicate` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Find.rux#L167)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type              | Description                     |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `items`     | `T[..]`           | the sequence to work on         |
| `predicate` | `func(T) -> bool` | the test each element is put to |

**Returns**: whether any element satisfies `predicate`; false for an empty sequence

<h2 id="none-of"><code>NoneOf&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func NoneOf<T>(items: T[..], predicate: func(T) -> bool) -> bool
```

Whether `predicate` accepts no element of `items`.
`items` is borrowed and read. An empty slice satisfies this, for the same reason it satisfies [`AllOf`](/docs/api/algorithms/searching#all-of).
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length, stopping at the first acceptance, and allocates nothing
beyond whatever `predicate` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Find.rux#L180)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type              | Description                     |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `items`     | `T[..]`           | the sequence to work on         |
| `predicate` | `func(T) -> bool` | the test each element is put to |

**Returns**: whether no element satisfies `predicate`; true for an empty sequence
